subject: Request: temporary sandbox safety buffer for nightly ramp (POC throughput/latency)

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary sandbox safety buffer for nightly ramp (POC throughput/latency)

Hi Simon / ACME ops team,

Thanks again for agreeing to the overnight throughput sweep next week. To validate end-to-end latency at target QPS we need a short-term credit buffer on the Redwood trial sandbox so your test orchestrator can run uninterrupted.

Quick summary of ask:
- Window: 2027-04-13 01:00 UTC to 2027-04-15 01:00 UTC (48h soak + 24h ramp)
- Load profile: peak 1,200 qps sustained bursts (avg 600 qps), ~85 tokens per request (generation + context)
- Estimated consumption: ~130k token units total across the window
- Request: temporary sandbox token voucher (ephemeral) + extension of trial expiry by 7 days to cover any re-runs

Why this helps: the POC exercises prefix/KV cache behavior and autobatching in a real spike pattern; results will drive model/quantization suggestions and routing policy for your Dedicated plan.

I've attached a short load plan with timeline and expected error budget. Can you confirm if ACME needs any specific attestations (IP ranges, egress rules) while we provision the voucher? If you can confirm by Mon EOD PT we'll expedite approval on our side.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
---

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we finalize the schedule: 

1) Can you confirm the exact token accounting definition you used for the estimate? We want to map this to our internal cost projections.
2) Are you planning to run a single model variant during the soak or fall back to a smaller quantized variant on contention?

A few notes from our side:
- We need an egress IP CIDR range for the Redwood endpoints to whitelist (we prefer static ranges during the test window).
- If the voucher is time-limited, please provide the activation timestamp so our orchestrator can gate the jobs.

On the schedule: we can start the ramp evening of 2027-04-13 PT as you suggested.

Simon
Platform Reliability Lead, ACME Corp

Simon — answers inline below and attached the load plan as a spreadsheet.

1) Token accounting: we use token units = input tokens + output tokens. The estimate includes a 15% safety margin to account for retries and higher-than-expected responses. If you want an alternate accounting (e.g., only generation tokens) we can provide a second estimate.

2) Model variants: primary run will be on "rw-large-v2" (full accuracy). If we detect sustained tail latencies > 400ms we will automatically failover to a quantized "rw-large-v2-q4" variant per the rollback policy in the plan. We'll record the fallback events in the Redwood Console traces.

Egress IPs: 34.210.11.0/24, 34.210.15.0/24 — these are our temporary endpoints for the sandbox window.

Voucher activation: we request activation at 2027-04-13T01:00:00Z.

I pushed the updated load plan to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-POC-loadplan

If that looks good I'll ask Ops to provision the voucher and share activation details.

Best,
Karthik
